ash: Quickstart trouble — first API call from my sample app returns an HTML 502, but the same token in the Console looks accepted. anyone seen this?

ash: command I run: `node quickstart/index.js` with `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in env. Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: text/html

<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

frank: Is that a workspace token or a service key? 502 is usually a gateway/proxy issue, not auth.

ash: workspace token created from Console -> API tokens. I tried a service key and inside the app it produced 403. From my laptop curl with workspace token I get 402 JSON: `{"error":"org_billing_required"}`. So host shows 402, app shows 502.

nina: This pattern often means an intermediate proxy or container runtime is stripping the `Authorization` header. When the SDK retries, a different path can return a generic HTML 502 and hide the real 402.

onboard-bot: Notice: Your org (acme-trial) does not have a billing method on file. First outbound requests may be blocked. Add billing at https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-trial/billing :credit_card:

ash: interesting — the Console quickstart flow didn't surface a billing modal for me, so I assumed the token was fully valid.

frank: try `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"input":"hi"}'` from both host and the runtime environment to compare headers and responses.

ash: host curl -> 402 with JSON referencing `org_billing_required`. inside runtime -> 502 HTML.

nina: workaround: mount a service key file into the runtime and set `REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat /run/creds/service_key)` inside the process; some proxies leave in-file injection intact. Also try `--network=host` or bypass corporate proxies to confirm.

frank: action items: 1) devex: add a preflight billing check in CLI/quickstart to show an explicit billing-required message before doing generation calls; 2) SDK: map known 502+HTML gateway patterns to the underlying 402/org_billing_required hint so DX isn't blocked by opaque HTML; 3) docs: add note about proxies/sidecars that drop Authorization and recommended secret-file mount patterns for CI/containers.

ash: confirmed workaround (mounted service key file) returns 402 JSON and shows the billing link. filing an eng/devex ticket with minimal repro, host vs runtime curl outputs, and the Dockerfile. tagging @frank @nina. thanks! :thumbsup:
